name: intel_pmu_disable_event
prose: Disables a perf event according to event->hw.idx, takes no lock itself, and returns nothing. Idx in 0..INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED-1: clears bit idx in this CPU's intel_ctrl_guest_mask, intel_ctrl_host_mask and intel_cp_status, then calls x86_pmu_disable_event. Idx in INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED..INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_BTS-1 or INTEL_PMC_IDX_METRIC_BASE..INTEL_PMC_IDX_METRIC_END: calls intel_pmu_disable_fixed, which for a TopDown idx returns without changing anything when other TopDown events are still set in active_mask (otherwise it switches to the SLOTS index), and otherwise clears the three masks for that index and clears that fixed counter's control bits in cpuc->fixed_ctrl_val; it does not itself write an MSR. Idx == INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_BTS: calls intel_pmu_disable_bts and intel_pmu_drain_bts_buffer and returns at once, skipping the PEBS step. Idx == INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_VLBR: clears the three masks for idx, then continues to the PEBS step below. Any other idx: clears the three masks for idx, prints a warning about the invalid index and returns at once, skipping the PEBS step. After every case except BTS and the invalid index, if event->attr.precise_ip is nonzero it calls the x86_pmu_pebs_disable static call for the event.
note: Reviewer round 1 (invalid idx clears masks before warning) right: core.c:2589-2592. Round 15 (FIXED_VLBR falls through to PEBS disable) right: core.c:2585-2587 break, then 2599-2600. Prose reworded to state it explicitly; also states intel_pmu_disable_fixed only updates fixed_ctrl_val (core.c:2561-2564), it does not write an MSR.

name: handle_pmi_common
prose: Handles the common part of a PMI on the current CPU. It increments the apic_perf_irqs IRQ stat and works on its own copy of status (passed by value). It returns 0 at once if status is zero after clearing GLOBAL_STATUS_COND_CHG, GLOBAL_STATUS_ASIF and GLOBAL_STATUS_LBRS_FROZEN. Otherwise it clears from status the bits of PEBS-enabled counters (cpuc->pebs_enabled & x86_pmu.pebs_capable) and then handles three special bits, each adding 1 to the handled count and being cleared from status when it was set: PEBS buffer overflow (calls x86_pmu_handle_guest_pebs and the drain_pebs static call, writes MSR_IA32_PEBS_ENABLE if cpuc->pebs_enabled changed during the drain, and clears the perf-metrics overflow bit when cpuc->events[INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED_SLOTS] is non-NULL and is a PEBS counter group); Intel PT ToPA PMI (calls intel_pt_interrupt unless perf_guest_handle_intel_pt_intr() returns nonzero); perf-metrics overflow (calls the intel_pmu_update_topdown_event static call with NULL, NULL). It then masks status with the hybrid intel_ctrl and ORs in cpuc->intel_cp_status. For each set bit below X86_PMC_IDX_MAX it adds 1 to handled first, then skips the bit if it is not set in cpuc->active_mask or cpuc->events[bit] is NULL; otherwise, if the event is a PEBS counter group it calls x86_pmu.drain_pebs, and then calls intel_pmu_save_and_restart and only when that returns nonzero it initializes the sample data, saves the LBR branch stack if the event has a branch stack, and calls perf_event_overflow. It returns the handled count, which can be 0 even when status was nonzero at entry, and does not acknowledge the global status register itself.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: x86_pmu.drain_pebs for PEBS counter group is after the active_mask/NULL-event checks (core.c:3293-3318); old prose put the drain first. Round 2 (skips overflow when save_and_restart fails) already handled (core.c:3322-3323). Original-round claim about clearing regular bits no longer applies, prose makes no such claim.

name: intel_pmu_hw_config
prose: Validates and configures a perf event for the Intel PMU and returns 0 or a negative errno; on an error return the event may already have been partly modified. It first returns any error from x86_pmu_hw_config and intel_pmu_bts_config. With attr.freq and attr.sample_freq set it initializes sample_period, last_period and period_left from intel_pmu_freq_start_period. With attr.precise_ip set it returns -EINVAL for the VLBR event config, sets PERF_X86_EVENT_AUTO_RELOAD (and, when the sample type and aux action allow, PERF_X86_EVENT_LARGE_PEBS and PERF_ATTACH_SCHED_CB) when neither freq nor wakeup_events without watermark is requested, and calls x86_pmu.pebs_aliases if present. It sets PERF_X86_EVENT_NEEDS_BRANCH_STACK for branch-stack sampling and, for branch-counter events, returns -EINVAL if the PMU lacks PMU_FL_BR_CNTR, the config has bits outside INTEL_ARCH_EVENT_MASK, a group member cannot take a branch-counter constraint, the counter count exceeds fls(x86_pmu.lbr_counters), or the leader is not a branch-stack event. When a branch stack is needed it sets up the LBR filter (returning its error), sets PERF_ATTACH_SCHED_CB, and unless BTS is in use takes the LBR exclusive reference (-EBUSY on conflict) and sets event->destroy. It returns -EINVAL for aux_output without precise_ip, otherwise sets PERF_X86_EVENT_PEBS_VIA_PT, may flag the group leader with PERF_X86_EVENT_PEBS_CNTR, and for an ACR group returns -EINVAL for metric events, freq mode, config2 with precise_ip above 2, sample_period above max_period, non-x86 leaders, non-x86 events between ACR events, or too many cause/counter bits, and otherwise sets the ACR counter constraints and PERF_X86_EVENT_ACR on the leader. For PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE and PERF_TYPE_HW_CACHE it returns 0 here. For TopDown slots/metric events it returns -EINVAL for disallowed config1, config2 or filter flags, and for metric events that sample or whose leader is not a non-sampling slots event, and otherwise marks the group PERF_X86_EVENT_TOPDOWN. For a load-latency event that needs the memory-loads auxiliary event it returns -ENODATA if the event is its own leader or no auxiliary event precedes it in the group. Finally, if the config lacks ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTSEL_ANY it returns 0; otherwise it returns -EINVAL when x86_pmu.version < 3, returns the error of perf_allow_cpu() if nonzero, and else sets ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTSEL_ANY in hw.config and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: slice 4477-4733 starts inside intel_pmu_hw_config (defined core.c:4283, ends 4605); real name used. Old prose claimed errors leave the event unmodified, which is false: flags, hw.config/period, attach_state, destroy and the exclusive-LBR count are set before later error returns (core.c:4294-4400).

name: precise_store_data
prose: Pure helper that turns a PEBS store data-source status word into a perf memory data-source encoding. It starts from PERF_MEM_S values OP=STORE, SNOOP=NA, LVL=L1 and TLB=L2 (0x40080104 together), then ORs in TLB=MISS (0x10000000) if bit 4 of status is set or TLB=HIT (0x8000000) otherwise, LVL=HIT (0x40) if bit 0 is set or LVL=MISS (0x80) otherwise, and LOCK=LOCKED (0x2000000) if bit 5 is set. Any 64-bit status is accepted, other status bits are ignored, and it reads or writes no state besides its argument.
note: All four reviewer claims wrong: constants checked against include/uapi/linux/perf_event.h:1339-1430 and ds.c:231-267. OP_STORE 4<<0, SNOOP_NA 1<<19=0x80000, LVL_L1 8<<5=0x100, TLB_L2 0x10<<26=0x40000000 -> base 0x40080104; TLB_MISS 4<<26=0x10000000, TLB_HIT 2<<26=0x8000000; LVL_HIT 2<<5=0x40, LVL_MISS 4<<5=0x80; LOCK_LOCKED 2<<24=0x2000000. Bits per union intel_x86_pebs_dse (st_l1d_hit bit0, st_stlb_miss bit4, st_locked bit5), ds.c:47-51.

name: imc_uncore_pci_init
prose: Calls imc_uncore_find_dev(), which tries snb_pci2phy_map_init(p->pci_id) for each entry of desktop_imc_pci_ids in order until one returns 0 and then returns that entry's PCI driver, or returns NULL if none succeeds (those calls can have effects of their own). If the driver is NULL it returns -ENODEV and does not write uncore_pci_uncores or uncore_pci_driver. Otherwise it sets uncore_pci_uncores to snb_pci_uncores, sets uncore_pci_driver to the found driver and returns 0.
note: Prose already correct; made imc_uncore_find_dev behaviour explicit (uncore_snb.c:1248-1272): it calls snb_pci2phy_map_init for each desktop_imc_pci_ids entry until one returns 0, which has its own side effects. -ENODEV is -19 as in the old prose; contract left empty because it writes globals.

name: branch_type
prose: Wrapper that returns get_branch_type(from, to, abort, false, NULL), so no fusion handling is done and no offset is written. get_branch_type computes the target privilege bit to_plm (X86_BR_KERNEL if to is a kernel address, else X86_BR_USER). It returns X86_BR_NONE if from or to is 0. Otherwise, if abort is nonzero, it returns X86_BR_ABORT | to_plm without examining any instruction. Otherwise, for a user from address it returns X86_BR_NONE if current->mm is NULL or copy_from_user_nmi copies zero bytes of the instruction; for a kernel from address it returns X86_BR_NONE unless from is a kernel text address outside the gate area. It then decodes the branch type of the instruction at from (decode result X86_BR_ABORT if the opcode or ModRM bytes cannot be decoded, X86_BR_NONE for non-branch or unknown opcodes). If from is a user address and to is a kernel address and the decoded type is neither X86_BR_SYSCALL nor X86_BR_INT, the type becomes X86_BR_IRQ, including when it was NONE or ABORT. If the final type is not X86_BR_NONE it is ORed with to_plm and returned, otherwise X86_BR_NONE is returned. It reads user memory through copy_from_user_nmi but allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: Reviewers round 1/15 right on ordering: abort is tested at utils.c:113 before the address validity checks at 116-151, so abort returns ABORT|to_plm even for user/kernel addresses; old prose put the NONE checks first. Round 2 (decode failure can become IRQ) right: utils.c:194-196. branch_type is a wrapper (utils.c:208-211) calling get_branch_type(from,to,abort,false,NULL).

name: zhaoxin_pmu_init
prose: Boot-time initialization of the Zhaoxin PMU; returns 0 or -ENODEV. It prints a message, reads CPUID leaf 10, and returns -ENODEV without changing x86_pmu if eax.mask_length is below ARCH_PERFMON_EVENTS_COUNT - 1 or version_id is not 2. Otherwise it copies zhaoxin_pmu into x86_pmu, fills version, cntr_mask64, cntval_bits, cntval_mask, events_maskl, events_mask_len and fixed_cntr_mask64 from CPUID, and registers zhaoxin_arch_events_quirk. It then switches on boot_cpu_data.x86. Family 6: if model is 0x0f with stepping at least 0x0e, or model is 0x19, it sets max_period to cntval_mask >> 1, enabled_ack to 1, uses zxc_event_constraints and zeroes the INSTRUCTIONS, CACHE_REFERENCES, CACHE_MISSES and BUS_CYCLES entries of zx_pmon_event_map; any other family 6 CPU returns -ENODEV. Family 7: sets the stalled-cycles entries of zx_pmon_event_map, and for model 0x1b or 0x3b copies the ZXD or ZXE hw_cache_event_ids, uses zxd_event_constraints and sets the branch entries; any other model returns -ENODEV. Any other family returns -ENODEV. In the -ENODEV returns after the CPUID checks, x86_pmu has already been overwritten and the quirk registered. On success it sets intel_ctrl to cntr_mask64 | (fixed_cntr_mask64 << INTEL_PMC_IDX_FIXED) and, if event_constraints is set, ORs cntr_mask64 into each constraint's idxmsk64 and adds x86_pmu_num_counters(NULL) to its weight, then returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head: function is defined at zhaoxin/core.c:505-618. Prior prose checked against code and kept, with the family/model enumeration and failure side effects re-verified (core.c:520-617). Reviewer round 15 only criticised the contract; contract dropped (writes globals).

name: local_db_save
prose: Saves and disables hardware breakpoints, returning the value to pass to local_db_restore. If the CPU has X86_FEATURE_HYPERVISOR and the per-CPU cpu_dr7 has no DR_GLOBAL_ENABLE_MASK bit set (hw_breakpoint_active() is false), it returns 0 without reading or writing DR7. Otherwise it reads DR7, clears the DR7_FIXED_1 bit in the value read, writes DR7_FIXED_1 to DR7 only if the cleared value is nonzero, executes a compiler barrier and returns the cleared value. In both paths the returned value has the DR7_FIXED_1 bit clear. It reads cpu_dr7 but takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 right that it reads per-CPU cpu_dr7 via hw_breakpoint_active (debugreg.h:121-124,132); old prose said no memory involved. Prose now says it reads that variable. Early return 0 without reading DR7 re-verified at 132-133; DR7 write only if dr7 nonzero after masking (138-140).

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (inb_p for u8, inw_p for u16, inl_p for u32): static inline function taking a u16 port. It reads the port with the matching inb/inw/inl, then calls slow_down_io(), then returns the value read.
note: Macro-generated: BUILDIO(b, u8), BUILDIO(w, u16), BUILDIO(l, u32) at io.h:307-309 define inb_p/inw_p/inl_p (io.h:268-273). Old prose missing the delay call ordering; no reviewer claim to check beyond name. Real function names put in prose.

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (outb_p, outw_p, outl_p): static inline function taking the value (u8, u16 or u32) and a u16 port. It writes the value to the port with the matching outb/outw/outl and then calls slow_down_io(). It returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated outb_p/outw_p/outl_p (io.h:262-266).

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (outsb, outsw, outsl): static inline function outs##bwl(u16 port, const void *addr, unsigned long count). If cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_GUEST_UNROLL_STRING_IO) is true it loops count times, writing the next element of that width from addr to the port with outb/outw/outl and advancing the pointer. Otherwise it executes a single 'rep outs' instruction with count repetitions (asm with memory clobber, advancing addr and counting count down). In both cases it reads count elements from addr, and nothing is done when count is 0. It returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated outsb/outsw/outsl (io.h:275-289). Old prose only described the guest-unroll path.

name: BUILDIO(bwl, type)
prose: Generated by the BUILDIO macro for each width (insb, insw, insl): static inline function ins##bwl(u16 port, void *addr, unsigned long count). If cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_GUEST_UNROLL_STRING_IO) is true it loops count times, reading from the port with inb/inw/inl and storing each element at the advancing addr. Otherwise it executes a single 'rep ins' instruction with count repetitions (asm with memory clobber). In both cases it stores count elements at addr, and nothing is done when count is 0. It returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated insb/insw/insl (io.h:291-305). Old prose only described the guest-unroll path.

name: smap_save
prose: Static inline function that runs an inline-asm alternative selected by X86_FEATURE_SMAP and returns the unsigned long flags. If the CPU has X86_FEATURE_SMAP, the patched code executes pushf, pop into flags, then clac: flags receives the EFLAGS value from before the clac, and clac clears the AC flag, so SMAP checks apply to supervisor accesses to user pages. If the feature is absent the alternative is empty, so the asm writes nothing and the returned local variable flags, which is never initialized in C, has an unspecified value. The asm declares memory and condition-code clobbers. It takes no locks.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: CLAC clears EFLAGS.AC, which makes SMAP enforcement apply to supervisor accesses to user pages; old prose said it disabled the protection (smap.h:38-49). Also removed the 'never fails' claim. Uninitialised flags when SMAP feature absent is per code: asm writes nothing then (smap.h:40-48).

name: vmware_hypercall1
prose: Static inline function that makes a VMware low-bandwidth hypercall with command cmd and one input in1 (passed in the arg1 register; arg3 is 0, and the ABI comment says the hypervisor uses only the low 32 bits of arguments on x86_64) and returns the unsigned long result. If the CPU feature X86_FEATURE_TDX_GUEST is enabled it returns vmware_tdx_hypercall(cmd, in1, 0, 0, 0, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL). Otherwise, if alternatives_patched is false and the code is not built as a module, it returns vmware_hypercall_slow(cmd, in1, 0, 0, 0, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL). Otherwise it executes the VMWARE_HYPERCALL inline asm (an I/O port IN on VMWARE_HYPERVISOR_PORT, vmcall or vmmcall depending on the patched alternative) with VMWARE_HYPERVISOR_MAGIC in the arg0 register, and returns the value the asm leaves in the arg0 register. The asm clobbers condition codes and memory, so memory may be modified.
note: Reviewer claims partly right: asm clobbers memory and cc (vmware.h:118) so 'no other state' is not claimed; the [0,2^32-1] range claim is not supported by the code (out0 is unsigned long, vmware.h:101,119; return values of vmware_tdx_hypercall/vmware_hypercall_slow are unconstrained in this file), so removed. Slow path is only taken when alternatives are not yet patched and not built as MODULE (vmware.h:107).

name: mfn_to_pfn
prose: Static inline function that converts a machine frame number to a pseudo-physical frame number. If xen_pv_domain() is false it returns mfn unchanged. Otherwise it first computes pfn with mfn_to_pfn_no_overrides: ~0 if mfn >= machine_to_phys_nr or if the fault-safe read of machine_to_phys_mapping[mfn] faults, else the value read. If __pfn_to_mfn(pfn) is not equal to mfn, pfn is set to ~0. Then, if pfn is ~0 and __pfn_to_mfn(mfn) equals IDENTITY_FRAME(mfn), pfn is set to mfn. It returns pfn, so the result is ~0 when no mapping is found and mfn is not an identity frame, and mfn itself for an identity frame even when mfn >= machine_to_phys_nr. This function itself takes no lock; the callees it uses are not defined in this slice.
note: All reviewer claims about ~0 vs identity frame are wrong against the existing prose: it already states the identity-frame fallback; code page.h:204-228 (line 224-225 identity fallback). Edit: replaced the 'acquires no locks' claim (callees __pfn_to_mfn/get_phys_to_machine unseen here) and stated the PV test.

name: gfn_to_pfn
prose: Static inline function that converts a guest frame number to a pseudo-physical frame number. If xen_pv_domain() is false it returns gfn unchanged; otherwise it returns mfn_to_pfn(gfn). In that PV case the result is the pfn read from machine_to_phys_mapping[gfn] when gfn < machine_to_phys_nr, the read does not fault and __pfn_to_mfn of that value equals gfn; otherwise gfn itself if __pfn_to_mfn(gfn) equals IDENTITY_FRAME(gfn); otherwise ~0. This function itself takes no lock.
note: Reviewer claims wrong: existing prose already covers identity fallback; gfn_to_pfn is page.h:251-257, simply mfn_to_pfn in PV. Same lock wording change as mfn_to_pfn.

name: amd_set_subcaches
prose: Sets the L3 subcache mask for the CPU cpu; cpu must be a valid CPU number because topology_amd_node_id(cpu) is evaluated first and cpu_data(cpu) is used later. It returns -EINVAL, without any PCI config access, if AMD_NB_L3_PARTITIONING is not set or mask > 0xf. Otherwise (the northbridge nb for the CPU's node must be non-NULL) it does the following. If the static reset variable is 0, it reads link register 0x1d4 into reset and misc register 0x1b8 masked with 0x180000 into ban. If mask != 0xf it clears the bits 0x180000 of misc register 0x1b8. It computes (mask << (4 * core_id)) | ((0xf ^ (1 << core_id)) << 26) and writes it to link register 0x1d4. It reads link register 0x1d4 back and, if it equals reset, rewrites misc register 0x1b8 with its 0x180000 bits cleared and then ORed with ban. It then returns 0. No other return value is possible.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: node_to_amd_nb(topology_amd_node_id(cpu)) and the later cpu_data(cpu) use cpu (amd_nb.c:187,207), so cpu must be valid; old prose said any cpu accepted. Round 2 claim (NULL always crashes) not claimed by prose; early -EINVAL returns before nb is dereferenced (191-192) so NULL nb only matters past that check.

name: suspend
prose: Runs an APM suspend and resume sequence and returns 0 or -EIO; the vetoable argument is not used. It calls dpm_suspend_start and dpm_suspend_end (their results are ignored). With local IRQs disabled it calls syscore_suspend and then enables IRQs again. With IRQs enabled it calls save_processor_state, then set_system_power_state(APM_STATE_SUSPEND), then sets ignore_normal_resume to 1 and calls restore_processor_state. It then disables local IRQs, calls reinit_timer, treats APM_NO_ERROR as APM_SUCCESS, calls apm_error('suspend', err) for any other non-success BIOS result, and sets the result to 0 for APM_SUCCESS and to -EIO otherwise. It calls syscore_resume with IRQs disabled, enables IRQs, and calls dpm_resume_start and dpm_resume_end. It then calls queue_event(APM_NORMAL_RESUME, NULL), which, when user_list is non-NULL, appends the event only to users whose reader flag is set and wakes apm_waitqueue. Under user_list_lock it sets suspend_wait to 0 and suspend_result to the result for each user on user_list, releases the lock, wakes apm_suspend_waitqueue and returns the result.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: local_irq_enable() at apm_32.c:1219 precedes set_system_power_state at 1222 (IRQs enabled during the BIOS call; restore_processor_state also with IRQs enabled); old prose said IRQs disabled around BIOS step. Round 2 right: queue_event skips users with !reader (apm_32.c:1156), and does nothing/wakes nothing when user_list is NULL (1153-1154).

name: sld_state_show
prose: Prints the split-lock and bus-lock detection mode for the boot CPU. It returns without printing if the boot CPU has neither X86_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECT nor X86_FEATURE_SPLIT_LOCK_DETECT. Otherwise it switches on sld_state. sld_off: prints 'disabled'. sld_warn: if X86_FEATURE_SPLIT_LOCK_DETECT is set it prints the #AC message and calls cpuhp_setup_state(CPUHP_AP_ONLINE_DYN, 'x86/splitlock', NULL, splitlock_cpu_offline), printing a warning if that returns a negative value and continuing; otherwise, if X86_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECT is set it prints the #DB warning message. sld_fatal: prints the #AC message if X86_FEATURE_SPLIT_LOCK_DETECT is set, otherwise the #DB message if X86_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECT is set. sld_ratelimit: prints the #DB rate-limit message (with bld_ratelimit.burst) only if X86_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECT is set, and prints nothing otherwise. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: sld_ratelimit prints only when X86_FEATURE_BUS_LOCK_DETECT is set (bus_lock.c:420-423), and sld_warn/sld_fatal print only on the matching feature, so 'otherwise prints a message' was too strong. Early return and cpuhp_setup_state in sld_warn re-verified at 393-395, 402-406.

name: get_block_address
prose: Returns the MSR address of threshold block 'block' of MCA bank 'bank' on cpu; high is unused. It returns 0 if bank >= per_cpu(mce_num_banks, cpu) or block >= NR_BLOCKS (5). If mce_flags.smca is set it returns MSR_AMD64_SMCA_MCx_MISC(bank) for block 0, returns 0 for a nonzero block when (low & MASK_BLKPTR_LO) is zero, and otherwise returns MSR_AMD64_SMCA_MCx_MISCy(bank, block - 1). Otherwise (legacy) it returns mca_msr_reg(bank, MCA_MISC) for block 0; for block 1 it computes offset = (low & MASK_BLKPTR_LO) >> 21 and returns MCG_XBLK_ADDR + offset if offset is nonzero and 0 if it is zero; and for blocks 2 to 4 it returns current_addr + 1 (as a 32-bit value). It takes no locks and has no other effects.
note: All reviewer claims wrong: addr is initialised to 0 and returned for invalid bank/block (amd.c:506-509), and block 1 with zero offset leaves addr 0 (526-530); only block >= 2 returns current_addr+1 (531-532). NR_BLOCKS is 5 (amd.c:29), MASK_BLKPTR_LO 0xFF000000 (amd.c:40), MCG_XBLK_ADDR 0xC0000400 (amd.c:41). Existing prose kept.

name: save_microcode_in_initrd
prose: Early-initcall function (no arguments) that returns 0 or -EINVAL. It returns 0, doing nothing else, if the microcode loader is disabled, the boot CPU vendor is not AMD, or the boot CPU family is below 0x10. Otherwise it reads CPUID leaf 1 eax and returns -EINVAL, without touching the equivalence table or patch cache, if find_blobs_in_containers finds no blob or scan_containers finds no microcode (desc.mc is NULL). Otherwise it calls _load_microcode_amd for the boot CPU's family, which frees any old equivalence table, scans the blob and adds patches to the cache, and calls cleanup() (discarding the cache and table) if the result is not UCODE_OK. It returns -EINVAL if that result is greater than UCODE_UPDATED, which includes UCODE_ERROR, and 0 otherwise, which includes a successful UCODE_OK load.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: UCODE_ERROR is after UCODE_UPDATED in enum ucode_state (internal.h:13-19), so 'ret > UCODE_UPDATED' (amd.c:1218) returns -EINVAL for an error; old prose said 0. __load_microcode_amd only returns UCODE_OK or UCODE_ERROR (amd.c:1122-1153). Round 2 right on the early returns not freeing the equiv table (1210-1215); prose already says so.

name: within_area
prose: Pure inline helper that returns true if and only if end >= base and addr < (base + size), where the addition is done in unsigned long arithmetic and so wraps modulo 2^64 on 64-bit builds. When base + size does not wrap and addr <= end, this is the test of whether the closed range [addr, end] overlaps the half-open area [base, base + size). It reads only its arguments and has no side effects.
note: Prose already correct (hw_breakpoint.c:253-257: end >= base && addr < (base + size) with unsigned wraparound). Reviewer claims about wraparound already stated in prose; random-test failure was in the contract only, so contract dropped.

name: ksys_ioperm
prose: The definition shown here is the one used when CONFIG_X86_IOPL_IOPERM is not set: it ignores from, num and turn_on, has no other effect and returns -ENOSYS (-38). When CONFIG_X86_IOPL_IOPERM is set, a different definition of ksys_ioperm applies.
note: Slice shows the CONFIG_X86_IOPL_IOPERM-not-set definition (ioport.c:205-209): returns -ENOSYS. With the option set, the real implementation at ioport.c:71 is used instead, so prose qualified. ENOSYS = 38.

name: mpparse_get_smp_config
prose: Parses the Intel MP configuration table (early or late pass, early nonzero meaning early). It returns at once, with no side effects, if smp_found_config is false, mpf_found is false, acpi_lapic is set and early is nonzero, or both acpi_lapic and acpi_ioapic are set. Otherwise it maps the floating pointer at mpf_base with early_memremap; if that fails it prints an error and returns. It prints the MPS version and, on 32-bit builds with CONFIG_X86_LOCAL_APIC, sets pic_mode to 1 if bit 7 of mpf->feature2 is set and to 0 otherwise. If mpf->feature1 is nonzero: with early nonzero it calls register_lapic_address(APIC_DEFAULT_PHYS_BASE) and skips to the unmap; with early zero it prints the default configuration number and calls construct_default_ISA_mptable(mpf->feature1). Otherwise, if mpf->physptr is nonzero it calls check_physptr and skips to the unmap if that returns nonzero (it always does for early nonzero, and also when the table has errors, in which case smp_found_config is cleared); if both feature1 and physptr are zero it calls BUG(). On the paths that do not skip, it prints the processor count only if early is zero and acpi_lapic is false. It unmaps the floating pointer on every path except BUG().
note: Reviewer round 15 right: Processors count is printed only when !early && !acpi_lapic (mpparse.c:533-534); old prose omitted !early. Round 1/2 claims already reflected in old prose (mapping failure, pic_mode conditional, default ISA table), re-verified mpparse.c:497-531.

name: filter_write
prose: Decides whether an MSR write to register reg is allowed. If allow_writes is MSR_WRITES_ON it returns 0. If allow_writes is MSR_WRITES_OFF it returns -EPERM. In the default mode (MSR_WRITES_DEFAULT) it calls __ratelimit on a static ratelimit state (one message per 30 seconds, burst 1), which updates that state and may take the state's internal lock; if the call says to suppress, it returns 0 without printing; otherwise it prints two warnings naming reg, the current command and pid, and returns 0. So it returns -EPERM exactly when allow_writes is MSR_WRITES_OFF and 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: in the default mode __ratelimit(&fw_rs) is called (msr.c:98), which uses the ratelimit state's internal lock, so 'acquiring no locks' was too strong. Return values verified at msr.c:93-105. Callers msr.c:122, 185.

name: find_oprom
prose: Searches the static adapter_rom_resources table for an option ROM that belongs to pdev and returns a pointer to its table entry, or NULL. It scans entries from index 0 and stops at the first entry whose end is 0 (it does not skip it). For each entry it maps start with isa_bus_to_virt, then reads with get_kernel_nofault the offset at rom+0x18, the vendor at rom+offset+0x4 and the device at rom+offset+0x6; if any of those reads faults it skips to the next entry. It returns the entry if match_id(pdev, vendor, device) is true, which holds when pdev has that vendor and device ids or when an entry of pdev's driver's id_table (if any driver and table exist) has them. Otherwise, if the list pointer at rom+offset+0x8 and the revision at rom+offset+0xc read successfully, rev >= 3, list is nonzero and probe_list finds a device in the list at rom+offset+list that match_id accepts, it returns the entry. If no entry matches it returns NULL. A non-NULL result points into the static table and must not be freed; the function has no other effects.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: match_id uses to_pci_driver(pdev->dev.driver) which is NULL-safe (include/linux/pci.h:999-1000: ( __drv ? container_of_const(...) : NULL )) and id_table loop guards NULL (probe_roms.c:84,90). Round 2 (stops at first zero-end entry) already stated in prose (probe_roms.c:125-126). Round 1 (id_table, rev>=3) already stated (143-146).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(ni_syscall)
prose: Generated by SYSCALL_DEFINE0(ni_syscall): the syscall body does nothing and returns -ENOSYS (-38). The x86 wrapper entry point __x64_sys_ni_syscall(const struct pt_regs *regs) is an alias of that body, so the pt_regs argument is not read; with IA32 emulation an __ia32_sys_ni_syscall alias is generated the same way.
note: Slice cut the head; the function is generated by SYSCALL_DEFINE0(ni_syscall) at process.c:1084-1087. x86 syscall wrapper: __SYS_STUB0 (syscall_wrapper.h:85-89) makes __x64_sys_ni_syscall(regs) an alias of the body, so regs is not read. Prose qualifies 'always'.

name: set_tsc_mode
prose: Sets the current thread's TSC access mode. If val equals PR_TSC_SIGSEGV (2) it calls disable_TSC, which, with preemption disabled, sets TIF_NOTSC and, only if the flag was not already set, sets CR4.TSD; it then returns 0. If val equals PR_TSC_ENABLE (1) it calls enable_TSC, which, with preemption disabled, clears TIF_NOTSC and, only if the flag was set, clears CR4.TSD; it then returns 0. For any other val it returns -EINVAL and changes nothing. Preemption is re-enabled before return and no lock is taken.
note: Prose checked against process.c:295-341: PR_TSC_ENABLE=1, PR_TSC_SIGSEGV=2; disable_TSC/enable_TSC use preempt_disable/enable only. Contract dropped (touches thread flags and CR4).

name: putreg32
prose: Writes a 32-bit ptrace register value for a 32-bit tracee. If regno is the offset of ebx, ecx, edx, edi, esi, ebp, eax, eip or esp in struct user32, it stores value in the matching pt_regs field and returns 0. For orig_eax it stores value in regs->orig_ax and, if syscall_get_nr(child, regs) is not -1, sets TS_I386_REGS_POKED in the child's thread status, then returns 0. For cs, ds, es and ss it returns the result of set_segment_reg. For fs and gs it calls set_segment_reg and, if that returns 0, also sets child->thread.fsbase or gsbase from x86_fsgsbase_read_task(child, value), returning the set_segment_reg result. For eflags it returns set_flags(child, value). For any regno from offsetof(u_debugreg[0]) to offsetof(u_debugreg[7]) inclusive, aligned or not, it returns ptrace_set_debugreg(child, (regno - offsetof(u_debugreg[0])) / 4, value). For any other regno it returns -EIO, writing nothing, if regno > sizeof(struct user32) or regno is not a multiple of 4, and otherwise (a dummy field, including regno == sizeof(struct user32)) writes nothing and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the debug register index is (regno - offsetof(struct user32, u_debugreg[0])) / 4, because regno is reduced before the call (ptrace.c:942-943); old prose said regno/4. Round 2 (unaligned regno in the debug range is accepted) already stated; dummy-field and regno==sizeof returning 0 (946-955) already stated. SEG32 cases: cs, ds, es, ss; fs/gs update bases (891-907).

name: getreg32
prose: Reads a 32-bit ptrace register value for a 32-bit tracee into *val. For cs, ss, ebx, ecx, edx, edi, esi, ebp, eax, orig_eax, eip and esp it stores the matching pt_regs field (truncated to 32 bits) in *val and returns 0. For ds, es, fs and gs it stores get_segment_reg(child, ...) in *val and returns 0. For eflags it stores get_flags(child) in *val and returns 0. For any regno from offsetof(u_debugreg[0]) to offsetof(u_debugreg[7]) inclusive, aligned or not, it stores ptrace_get_debugreg(child, (regno - offsetof(u_debugreg[0])) / 4), truncated to 32 bits, in *val and returns 0. For any other regno it returns -EIO, leaving *val unwritten, if regno > sizeof(struct user32) or regno is not a multiple of 4, and otherwise (a dummy field, including regno == sizeof(struct user32)) stores 0 in *val and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: debug register index is (regno - offsetof(u_debugreg[0])) / 4 (ptrace.c:1001-1002); old prose said regno/4. Round 2 (unaligned debug range accepted) and round 1 (regno==sizeof accepted giving 0) already stated. R32/SEG32 cases verified ptrace.c:977-993.
